title: Brandy Walker named finalist for Teacher of the Year at Cooke STEM Academy
text:
Brandy Walker named finalist for Teacher of the Year at Cooke STEM Academy
Brandy Walker, a fifth-grade English Language Arts and social studies teacher at Cooke STEM Academy, was named a Teacher of the Year finalist as part of Detroit Public Schools Community District’s Educators of the Year awards ceremony and luncheon, according to a June 10 announcement.
Walker has spent 26 years in the classroom, focusing on building confidence in her students through daily affirmations and consistent encouragement. She said, “If you are not affirmed at home, you’re going to get affirmed in room 214 in Walker’s classroom.” Her students recite affirmations, including the Room 214 pledge that encourages them to strive for excellence and remember they are destined for greatness.
Her recognition is supported by notable student achievements. This year marks her fifteenth consecutive National Association for the Advancement of Colored People essay contest winner in the fifth-grade division—a streak that began in 2012. Each year since then, her students have placed first, second, third or earned multiple placements in this competition. Additionally, she helped eleven students become published authors through the Detroit Writes contest this year; last year, fourteen students achieved this distinction.
Walker described her teaching style by saying: “I’m firm, but I’m fair. I push them. And I say, this is my bar. You have to meet me at the top.” She brings high expectations from her experience working at application and testing schools into Cooke STEM Academy because she believes excellence should not be limited to selective classrooms.
“All scholars can learn,” Walker said. “You don’t just have to go to one of those application testing schools to be a scholar. You don’t have to just go to one of those high-performing schools to be a high-achieving scholar. We have high-achieving scholars right here.”
Walker concluded by stating, “I do not lower my standards because they can, and they will, and they have been meeting me at the top.”
